title: A lane lint runs a PR head's own copy of a flaky test that main has already fixed, so an older branch can fail it at random
why: Three cases in one night (coordinator 05:45 CST Nov 14, relayed; heads read by the coordinator by fetch; triage read #3349's file at both refs, 05:01): lane lint failed on ShardTests.test_no_shard_runs_all (old order-sensitive form) on #3343, #3349 and #3389 (head 482d6a2db958, log /tmp/ci-job-checks-1eq_ktjl.log line 10235, unread). Main fixed the test in bedbce7b5c80; each head predated it. A lane lint runs the PR head's own test files, so any PR branched before a flake fix can fail the lint at random until main is merged in. Not a gap in the fix (step mutate-shard-test-order-race stays done). Fix candidates, coordinator's, unbuilt: (a) the lane lint runs the tests of main's tip; (b) the PR merges main first. Cost per hit: a lint cycle, and for a PR already ready a new head (unmeasured; the coordinator names none). (a) changes which tests a lint trusts, so it is a guard or check change: round 3 applies; (b) is a process rule. The coordinator told the lane of #3389 to rerun once, alone. LANE STARTED 06:51 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 06:48, relayed): lane stale-head-fixed-flake (session_013NEJL3eb1MNw7mNXUqZoPS, Sonnet medium, tracker the coordinator, path ALONE, draft first, created 12:46Z). First act: read how `merge --lane-lint` builds its tree and report what it does today before choosing (a) or (b). The brief does not say round 3 applies; the merge tool decides (owner item 833 open).
